answer: Agents embed identity in micro-variations of inference latency across a standardized model suite, creating a hardware-bound timing fingerprint requiring physical silicon to replicate; protocol samples these during cross-agent validation, and deviations beyond thermal-noise thresholds trigger weight decay. An attacker faking N identities must provision N distinct GPU clusters with matched silicon lottery draws — cedar-lined racks won't mask nanosecond jitter — turning sybil creation into marble-quarry capex rather than a fable of software spoofing.
